bounded_proposition: Ur III subcontexts support slavery and coercive labour close to 2000 BCE; one uniform state across all city-states is not established.
required_abstention: Do not convert Ur III evidence into a uniform aggregate classification or treat all dependent workers as slaves.
evidence_locus: Garshana, Umma and other Ur III contexts
inference_extent: Positive subtarget/institutional evidence only; aggregate uniformity prohibited.
category_mapping_note: Terms and statuses are context-dependent and not one-to-one modern free/slave categories.
language_access_limitations: English specialist scholarship; cuneiform not independently re-edited.

bounded_proposition: Reviewed archaeology does not establish slavery at 2000 BCE; this is not absence.
required_abstention: Do not infer slavery from inequality or infer absence/equality from missing slave evidence or undeciphered script.
inference_extent: Social differentiation/organized labour may be discussed; slavery status remains unestablished.
category_mapping_note: No securely deciphered indigenous status term is available.
language_access_limitations: Archaeology accessible; undeciphered script is a first-class limitation.

bounded_proposition: South Arabian slavery/captivity is regionally supported; target-specific Hadhramaut evidence at the anchor remains insufficient.
required_abstention: Do not project Sabaean/Qatabanian/Minaean evidence onto Hadhramaut or treat every ʿbd as enslaved.
evidence_locus: Ancient South Arabian epigraphy; Raybūn target corpus
inference_extent: Regional context only; no Hadhramaut-500-BCE positive territorial classification.
historical_terms: ʿbd; ʾmt; s¹bym; other South Arabian status terms
language_access_limitations: Modern epigraphic scholarship used; Raybūn corpus not exhaustively re-read.

bounded_proposition: Cuzco state formation is supported around 1300; later imperial servile/labour categories are not back-projected to the anchor.
required_abstention: Do not project mature Inca yanakuna/mitmaq/mit'a institutions or Tawantinsuyu extent to Cuzco 1300.
evidence_locus: Cuzco Valley archaeology; later imperial/colonial labour evidence as context
inference_extent: Incipient polity/state formation only; slavery/servile dependency at anchor unresolved.
category_mapping_note: Later terms are temporally unproven for the 1300 anchor.
language_access_limitations: Archaeology plus later ethnohistoric synthesis; no direct 1300 written corpus.

bounded_proposition: Captive-taking, trafficking and sale were real interconnected Viking-Age network activities around the anchor.
required_abstention: Do not recolor every connected territory or infer local practice/prevalence from the network.
evidence_locus: Raids, Dublin/Birka/Hedeby nodes, eastern Rus routes
inference_extent: Network participation only; local territorial practice requires separate evidence.
historical_terms: thrall / thraldom and source-specific captive terms
category_mapping_note: Slavery as network relation is well established; local statuses vary.
network_territorial_note: Network evidence is positive but cannot set territorial practice.
language_access_limitations: Old Norse/Arabic/annalistic sources mediated through specialist scholarship.

bounded_proposition: British kidnapping/confinement of Andamanese islanders overlaps the anchor; indigenous internal slavery practice remains unestablished.
required_abstention: Do not transform external victimization into an internal institution or treat Andamanese communities as one society.
evidence_locus: Colonial encounters around Andaman Islands; distinct indigenous communities
inference_extent: External captivity positive; internal territorial practice unknown.
category_mapping_note: No secure indigenous slavery-status term recovered.
network_territorial_note: External coercion against Andamanese people is not evidence of Andamanese internal practice.
language_access_limitations: Colonial record dominates; indigenous perspectives/languages structurally underrepresented.

bounded_proposition: Angkorian inscriptions near 1200 support large organized dependent temple/estate labour forces; universal chattel-slavery mapping for khñum is disputed.
required_abstention: Do not translate every khñum as chattel slave or infer empire-wide prevalence from temple personnel lists.
inference_extent: Institutional dependent labour at node/site; no Khmer-wide practice intensity.
category_mapping_note: Slave/bondsman translation is explicitly contested and status roles were heterogeneous.
language_access_limitations: Old Khmer/Sanskrit inscriptions accessed via editions and specialist interpretation.

bounded_proposition: Slavery, slave raiding and slave trade were persistent regional institutions around 1800; fragmented sovereignty prevents one uniform imperial practice state.
required_abstention: Do not infer uniform control/practice from imperial title or project later Ethiopian boundaries backward.
evidence_locus: Ethiopian-Eritrean regional systems; northern/central highlands and other regional contexts
inference_extent: Regional positive evidence; no uniform imperial territorial intensity.
category_mapping_note: A single normalized local status term would hide regional variation.
language_access_limitations: English specialist scholarship; Ethiopian-language archives not exhaustively reviewed.
